pending.body: In `gh_mineral_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1639-1641), the floor value 0.3 is hardcoded in both the low-GH and high-GH branches, while the parallel `molt_mineral_modifier()` (shrimp.rs:1690) uses the tunable `params.molt_mineral_factor_floor`. If a user tunes `molt_mineral_factor_floor` to a different value, molt and reproduction GH penalties will diverge silently. Either: (a) add a dedicated `repro_mineral_factor_floor` parameter, or (b) reuse `molt_mineral_factor_floor` in `gh_mineral_factor()` and document that it controls both domains.

In `tan_repro_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1619) and `no2_repro_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1630), the slope of suppression is computed as `threshold * 2.0`, meaning full suppression always occurs at 2× the threshold concentration. This implicit doubling rule is not exposed as a tunable parameter. Add explicit `tan_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l` and `no2_repro_full_suppression_mg_n_per_l` parameters (defaulting to 2.0 and 1.0 respectively) so the suppression curve shape can be tuned independently of the onset threshold.

In `temp_repro_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1546-1549), the cold-temperature offset `4.0` (which defines the width of the ramp from 0.1 to 1.0 below `optimal_temp_min_c`) is hardcoded. Similarly, the piecewise slopes 0.5 and 0.45 (lines 1554, 1557) and the minimum values 0.1 and 0.05 (lines 1547, 1559) are all hardcoded. These shape the temperature-reproduction curve but cannot be tuned via species data. At minimum, document these as intentionally fixed; ideally, extract the cold-offset width as a named parameter.

In `gh_mineral_factor()` (shrimp.rs:1641), the high-GH penalty divisor is hardcoded as `10.0`: `(1.0 - (gh_d - params.gh_max_d) / 10.0)`. The molt system has a tunable `molt_gh_excess_penalty_divisor` for the analogous calculation. Use a corresponding named parameter for the reproduction GH excess curve.
